methods: Rapid literature review
Systematic literature review
In vitro risk assessment studies: Pathogen isolation, cell cultures, organoids, tissue and primary cell studies
Molecular -biological-, biochemical and biophysical studies
Studies in animal models: Transmission models, pathogenesis studies
In vitro risk assessment studies: Mechanical intervention experiments; Disinfection/surface inactivation studies
Studies in animal models: Vaccine challenge studies; Therapeutic efficacy studies
((Unbiased)Metagenomic) sequencing; Diagnostic testing (molecular, antigen, serology, neutralisation)
Surveys / questionnaires: Cross-sectional surveys, targeted subgroup surveys
Panel studies
Qualitative studies: Focus groups; (In-depth) interviews; Case studies; Community/ ethnographic observation
Behavioural tracking: Mobility data, compliance observations
Network analysis
(Social) media analytics: Social listening / Sentiment analysis; Misinformation tracking; Media coverage analysis
Experiments (RCTs / online / field): Scenario Experiments; Communication experiments; Other behavioural interventions
Quasi-experiments / Natural experiments: Implementation trials; Operational pilots
Participatory and co-creation studies
Descriptive outbreak studies: early case descriptions; clustering; exposure data; genomics
(Routine) surveillance data: national surveillance; contact- tracing; laboratory reporting systems; genomic epidemiology
Cross-sectional studies: general population; subpopulations e.g. schools, healthcare workers; animals; products
Case-control studies (in humans; animals)
Cohort studies: Retrospective; prospective, in animals, sub-populations (households, schools, healthcare workers, patients, general population)
(Semi-randomized) intervention trials: in humans, animals, settings; treatment testing; intervention testing; implementation evaluation
Data analysis: Socio-economic registries studies; Socio-economic indicators; Vulnerability mapping
Health Systems Evaluation: Capacity assessments; Policy mapping
Economic modelling
Comparative studies (comparison of socio-economic effects across regions, countries, groups)
Policy evaluations (e.g., lockdowns, subsidies, school closures)
Natural experiments: Policy experiments / Operational pilots (variation in timing or exposure)
Case reports
Case series
Hospital registry studies
Healthcare workers studies
Clinical treatment trials
Branching process models: Galton-Watson processes
Compartmental models: deterministic or stochastic ODE-based SEIR models and variants
Individual-based models: agent-based models, network models
Statistical models: nowcasting, machine-learning methods
objectives: O1
Objective 1. To identify and characterise the pathogen
O2
Objective 2. To perform phenotypic characterisation of the pathogen
O3
Objective 3. To evaluate diagnostic test performance for pathogen detection and surveillance applications
O4
Objective 4. To characterise infection and replication dynamics, tissue and cellular tropism
O5
Objective 5. To characterise the reservoir and host range of the pathogen
O6
Objective 6. To characterise the routes of transmission
O7
Objective 7. To characterise immune response dynamics and population immunity
O8
Objective 8. To characterise environmental stability and inactivation of the pathogen
O9
Objective 9. To identify pathogen and host targets relevant for the development of diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines
Objective 10. To describe and reconstruct pathogen emergence and spread
Objective 11. To characterise key epidemiological parameters and project epidemic dynamics (in real-time)
Objective 12. To identify societal and biomedical risk factors, determinants, and drivers of exposure and infection
Objective 13. To characterise clinical presentation, disease course, severity, and clinical impact of infection
Objective 14. To evaluate the effectiveness of medical measures to counter the epidemic
Objective 15.  To evaluate the effectiveness of non-medical measures to counter the epidemic
Objective 16. To project epidemic trajectories and assess the impact and effects of the epidemic on society
Objective 17. To understand how citizens' (pre-existing) conditions, behaviours and perceptions determine the response to the epidemic
Objective 18. To identify patterns, drivers, and inequalities in risks, impact and intervention adherence across (vulnerable) populations
Objective 19. To characterise societal perceptions, attitudes and risk understanding related to the epidemic
Objective 20. To characterise communication dynamics, misinformation, and information dissemination across media ecosystems
Objective 21. To characterise public trust, institutional credibility, and governance dynamics during the epidemic
Objective 22. To characterise institutional capacity, preparedness, and system resilience in responding to the epidemic
Objective 23. To assess the societal, behavioural, and governance impacts of the epidemic and response measures across sectors and time horizons
Objective 24. To identify and evaluate strategies that can help mitigate the mental, social, economic and other societal effects of the epidemic and the countermeasures on citizens
Objective 25. To identify the strategies that can make communication and risk messaging more inclusive and effective
